{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Dessert|Dessert]] | [[Cookbook:Cake|Cake]] | [[Cookbook:New York City cuisine|New York City cuisine]]

Arnold Reuben, owner of Turf Restaurant at 49th and Broadway in New York City, developed the recipe for New York cheesecake in 1929 after eating a slice of cheese pie at a friend's home.<ref>[http://whatscookingamerica.net/History/Cakes/Cheesecake.htm Info on the history of cheesecake]</ref>

He altered his hostess’ recipe and eventually developed his own version of cheesecake which relies on cream cheese rather than cottage cheese as most other bakeries did at the time. Reuben then served his new creation in his restaurant which became a hit in no time.   

The below recipe makes a firm and heavy cheesecake, nicely flavored with [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemon]]. It is very important to avoid over beating the ingredients in order to avoid cracks.

==Ingredients==

=== Crust ===
*5 [[Cookbook:Ounce|ounces]] Barnham and Bailey animal crackers or sweet digestive biscuits
*3 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
*4 tablespoons melted [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]

=== Cake ===
*2 ½ [[Cookbook:Pound|pounds]] softened [[Cookbook:Cream Cheese|cream cheese]] 
*1 ¾ [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] white granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] [[Cookbook:Corn Starch|corn starch]]
*3 tablespoons [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]]
*[[Cookbook:Zest|Zest]] of 1 [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemon]] 
*1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Vanilla|vanilla]] 
*5 large whole [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]]
*2 large egg yolks
*¼ cup [[Cookbook:Heavy Cream|heavy cream]]

==Procedure==

=== Crust ===
#Butter bottom and sides of [[Cookbook:Inch|10-inch]] [[Cookbook:Springform Pan|springform pan]].
#Crush animal crackers into a fine powder. Mix with 3 tablespoons of sugar.
#Add to melted butter and mix with a fork until blended.
#Press mixture into the bottom and up about one third of the sides of the pan.
#Refrigerate 1 hour.

=== Cake ===
#Have all ingredients at room temperature.
#Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to [[Cookbook:Oven Temperatures|475°F]]. 
#Mix sugar, flour and cornstarch together.
#Using a wooden spoon, [[Cookbook:Beating|beat]] cream cheese with sugar mix, zest and vanilla until it is smooth. Do not overbeat.
#Add the whole eggs and egg yolks, one at a time, beating lightly with wooden spoon after each addition. Do not overbeat as this causes the cheesecake to crack.
#Gently stir in cream.
#Pour mixture into the pan. Place pan on [[Cookbook:Cookie Sheet|cookie sheet]] to avoid leakage.
#[[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] at 475°F for 15 minutes 
#Lower heat to [[Cookbook:Oven Temperatures|225°F]] and bake for 1 hour
#Raise heat to [[Cookbook:Oven Temperatures|250°F]] and bake for about 15 more minutes
#Refrigerate immediately for at least 1 hour, covered with a cloth and [[Cookbook:Cookie Sheet|cookie sheet]] (cloth on bottom) until condensation stops forming. Condensation will drip onto the cake if you cover it right away with [[Cookbook:Plastic Wrap|plastic wrap]].

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* You may substitute lemon juice for vanilla.
